# Workflow diagram authoring

`docs/diagrams/` holds five workflow maps, each in two variants. The engineer version names classes, commands, services and stored procedures;
the plain-language version says the same in the words the people using the screens know. Each variant is published as a PDF in `pdf/<workflow>/` and described by a Graphviz source in
`dot/<workflow>/`. The workflow declared at the top of the spec names both folders, so one run cannot
write into another workflow's folder.
Everything in that folder except the JSON specs is build output.

## Edit the spec, never the output

| File | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/spec-diagram-*.json` | **Source of truth.** Edit this. |
| `tools/manifest.json` | Which spec builds which PDF. Edit only when a document is added or removed. |
| `diagram-*.dot` | Generated by `tools/dotgen.py` into `dot/<workflow>/`. Regenerated on every build — a hand edit is lost. |
| `diagram-*.pdf` | Generated by `tools/render_sheets.py` into `pdf/<workflow>/`. |
| `tools/diagram_context.py` | **Read-only.** Prints a workflow's sheets, nodes, edges, findings and connectors for an agent, from the manifest. Never writes to this folder. |
| `tools/*.py` | The pipeline. Change only when the *contract* changes, not to fit one sheet. |

```powershell
python docs\diagrams\tools\dotgen.py docs\diagrams\tools\spec-diagram-workorder-new-request.json
python docs\diagrams\tools\render_sheets.py docs\diagrams\tools\manifest.json
python docs\diagrams\tools\verify_pdfs.py
```

`dotgen.py` accepts any number of spec files; rebuilding every source is a loop over
`tools\spec-*.json`. A checkout may carry only some of the specs the manifest lists, so a loop over what is
present is the safe form. `verify_pdfs.py --no-png` skips the 300 DPI export when you only want the
assertions.

## Pitfalls in the build

- **`render_sheets.py` resolves each `spec` relative to the manifest's own folder.** Building a subset
  manifest in `%TEMP%` and leaving the bare file names in it fails with `FileNotFoundError` naming a path
  under `docs\diagrams\tools\`. Write absolute `spec` paths into a subset manifest.
- **`render_sheets.py` has no argument parser.** It takes the manifest path as `sys.argv[1]`, so `--help`
  is treated as a file name and raises `FileNotFoundError: '--help'`. Read this file instead.
- **The whole-manifest build needs every spec present.** `manifest.json` lists all ten documents, so
  `render_sheets.py docs\diagrams\tools\manifest.json` stops on the first spec this checkout does not have
  and writes nothing. Render only the workflow you changed, with a subset manifest, and say so; do not
  "fix" it by deleting other documents from `manifest.json`.
- **`verify_pdfs.py` does not count shapes.** It checks page size, margins and type size only, so a sheet
  that has grown to 17 nodes passes. Count the nodes yourself; when a finding would take a sheet past 16,
  fold related findings into the existing flag and re-word it rather than adding a box.
- **A `refactor` or `note` node must be attached.** `dotgen.py` warns when no edge touches a node, and an
  unattached finding has no place in the flow. Give it a plain edge from the element that shows the fault.
- **Lane placement decides the layout, not the node's meaning.** A finding put in the `ui` lane takes that
  lane's rank, stretches the row and drags edges across the sheet; the same finding in the lane that owns
  the code (`vm` for a view-model sentence, `data` for a read) settles the page. Render the page and look
  before believing a placement is fine.
- **`.dot` files are tracked but are build output.** Regenerating one is expected; a hand edit is lost on
  the next `dotgen.py` run.

## Consuming a diagram as implementation context

A diagram is also an input: it tells an agent what a workflow does before a UI/UX change is proposed.
Use the `workflow-diagram-context` skill for the procedure, and this command for the content:

```powershell
python docs\diagrams\tools\diagram_context.py --list
python docs\diagrams\tools\diagram_context.py --workflow workorder-new-request --sheet 3
```

The manifest (`tools/manifest.json`) is the index: it maps each workflow and variant to its spec and
PDF. The digest reads the spec as the source of truth, checks the `.dot` file against it, and reports a
missing spec, dot or PDF instead of implying it was read. A request is a reference to current behaviour;
it never authorises a change to that behaviour on its own.

When the diagram and the code disagree, report both — do not quietly draw the diagram to match a
change you have already made.

## The print contract

These numbers are the requirement, not a preference. A sheet that breaks one is not finished.

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Page | 792 × 612 pt — 11 in × 8.5 in, landscape |
| Margin | 0.5 in clear on all four sides; the header rule sits at y = 49, the legend rule at y = 555.5 |
| Type floor | 9.5 pt effective on every label, edge annotation and legend item; 11 pt for node labels whenever the sheet allows |
| Shapes per sheet | 12–16 |
| Canvas | pure white `#FFFFFF`, ink `#111111`, pastel fills, 1.5 pt borders |
| Every page | title header, `Sheet X of Y`, shape legend |

## Splitting a sheet

Never shrink type or tile a grid to force a flow onto one page. Split at an architectural seam — UI and
validation on one sheet, services and stores on the next — and join the halves with `conn` off-page
badges that name the command they resume at, for example `[To Sheet 3]\nSubmitAsync`. Both halves must
carry the badge: the reader arrives from the previous sheet, not just leaves toward the next.

## Labels

- Write deliberate breaks as `\n` inside the JSON string: `"Reads the press\nlist"`.
- Keep a line under about 30 characters and a node under 5 lines. The renderer wraps by measurement, so
  a long `sp_*` name will still fit, but a wrapped stored procedure reads badly — break it yourself.
- One idea per node. If a label needs "and", it is usually two nodes.
- Never widen a lane by hand to make a box fit; the grid sizes columns from content.

## Node kinds

`ui` view · `vm` view model · `svc` service · `db` stored procedure · `erp` Infor Visual shape ·
`mirror` `mtm_mock` fallback · `dec` decision · `note` callout · `refactor` finding · `conn` off-page.

## Refactor flags

A finding goes in a `refactor` node on the sheet that shows the code, and gets the same finding in plain
words on the matching friendly sheet. Keep the wording user-facing there — "Worth fixing: four saves
happen with no single undo if one fails", not a method name. Every flagged finding also belongs in
`docs/diagrams/diagram-workflow-refactor-notes.md`, which is the list a `/speckit.specify` run consumes.

- **Attach every flag.** Give the finding a plain edge from the node that shows the fault; `dotgen.py`
  warns about a node no edge touches, and an unattached finding has no place in the flow.
- **Put it in the lane that owns the code**, not the lane where the symptom is seen: a sentence written in
  a view model goes in `vm`, a bad read goes in `data`. A flag parked in `ui` takes that lane's rank,
  stretches the row and drags edges across the sheet.
- **One flag may carry related findings.** When a sheet is at the 12–16 shape ceiling, add the new defects
  to the existing flag's wording (four or five short lines) rather than adding a second box, and keep the
  friendly sheet's wording equivalent. Write each defect up separately in the notes file, as its own
  numbered section.
- **A flag's notes section is part of the change.** A finding that is only in a spec is a picture of a
  problem nobody can act on.

## Prohibited

- No `.cs` file, test, or inline SQL string added to the solution for diagram work. `InlineSqlAuditTests`
  and `RetiredSymbolAuditTests` are the guardrails, and diagrams are documentation.
- No raw PDF bytes written by hand, and no `reportlab`-style composition that bypasses the spec.
- Do not add a Markdown note per diagram. One README for the folder, one refactor note for the findings.

## Before claiming a sheet is done

1. `verify_pdfs.py` reports every page at size, in margin, and at or above the type floor.
2. You looked at the 300 DPI PNG of the page you changed — `%TEMP%\mtm-diagrams\png` — for a label
   sitting on a border, an arrow crossing a box, or a lane frame cutting a node.
3. A changed label still matches the code: class, command and stored-procedure names are read from the
   repository, never recalled.
